figures.caption: Fig. 1. A flowchart illustrates the modeling methodology.

Fig. 2. Histogram distributions of various features and target variables (RW: raw water, TW: treated water, MIN: minimum, MAX: maximum, SD: standard deviation, CV: coefficient of variation. Each subplot represents the distribution of sample points within a specific variable. The vertical axis reveals the occurrence frequency of each feature within the dataset, while the horizontal axis depicts the sample intervals. The purple line represents the fitted frequency distribution curve, which indicates the range of variable utilization within the dataset). (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

Fig. 3. Spearman rank correlation coefficient matrix between all input parameters and the target variable. Symbols with the suffix “RW” represent raw water quality indicators, while those with “TW” are for treated water.

Fig. 4. Fitting results and scatter density plots for the AutoML: RF model on training and testing sets. The Fig includes model performance plot for samples on the training set (a) and the testing set (b), and scatter plot of samples on the training set (c) and the testing set (d).
Fig. 5. Optimization results of PACl dosage using the AutoML: RF model for the Yangtze River source (a) and the Luanhe River source (b).

Fig. 6. SHAP feature importance (a) and summary plot (b) for the test set. The vertical axis of plot (a) represents the features in descending order of their average absolute SHAP value on the model output, with larger values indicating a higher contribution of the feature to the prediction, and the horizontal axis indicates the size of the SHAP value, reflecting the average degree of influence of the feature on the model output. Fig (b) each point represents the SHAP value of a sample, the position of the horizontal axis shows the size of the value, the colour shades reflect the original value of the feature is high or low (red is high value, blue is low value), the vertical axis represents the order by the importance of the feature, in line with Fig (a), the superimposed trend represents the relationship between the feature’s value high or low and the direction of the SHAP value that can be observed from the distribution of points. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)
context_mentions: T-RW, NTU-RW, WTR, NTU-TW, and pH-RW, as shown in Fig. 6(a).

figures.caption: Fig. 7. Nonlinear relationships between individual water quality parameters and coagulant dosage for EC-RW (a), pH-TW (b), NH3-N-RW (c), CODMn-RW (d), T-RW (e), NTU-RW (f), WTR (g), NTU-TW (h), and pH-RW (i). For each data point with a positive SHAP value, the dosage of coagulant increases with the SHAP value, exerting a positive impact. Conversely, for points with negative SHAP values, the opposite effect is observed. The units for these variables are consistent with those in Fig. 2.

Fig. 8. Decision plots and waterfall plots for two local samples, featuring three key characteristics: 1) the output value, representing the prediction for an individual sample; 2) the base value, corresponding to the average expected value in the testing set; and 3) colour coding, where red variables push the prediction upwards and blue variables push it downwards) are presented. The Fig includes decision plot (a) and waterfall plot (b) for a sample with dosing amount above the average, and decision plot (c) and waterfall plot (d) for a sample with dosing amount below the average. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)
